heading: Questions, answered.
description: Everything you need to know before you wire Helix into your workflow.

items.question: What is Helix, exactly?
items.answer: Helix is an AI orchestrator that turns a single prompt into atomic, verified code units. It plans the work, executes it unit-by-unit against your repo, and verifies every change before merge.

items.question: How is Helix different from a coding agent?
items.answer: A coding agent writes one big diff. Helix writes many small, scoped units — each type-checked, tested, and linted against the rest of your repo. Failures pause the loop, so main stays green.

items.question: Which languages and frameworks does Helix support?
items.answer: Helix is language-agnostic. It works with any repo that has a working type-check, test, and lint pipeline — TypeScript, Go, Python, Rust, and more.

items.question: Can I self-host Helix?
items.answer: Yes. Helix is open source and runs anywhere you can run Node.js — your laptop, a CI runner, or your own infrastructure.

items.question: How is Helix priced?
items.answer: Helix itself is open source and free. You bring your own model and your own compute — Helix orchestrates the loop.

items.question: Is Helix open source?
items.answer: Yes. The full source is on GitHub under a permissive license, and contributions are welcome.
